newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador top economic official to stay on - source.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador top economic official to stay on - source.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon Tuesday night rejected the resignation of Monetary Board President Danilo Carrera, a Central Bank source told Reuters.
"I have just received a call from the president of the Monetary Board from the government palace, where he tells me he has been ratified in office," the source said.
The Monetary Board sets economic policy.
Carrera had tendered his resignation earlier Tuesday over differences in economic policy, but it was up to Alarcon to accept or reject the offer.
The Central Bank source said Carrera had offered to bow out of the cabinet due to "a difference of opinion with the government over economic policy."

It was not immediately clear what these differences consisted of, but an announcement on new economic policy was expected this week and the government hinted it would adopt only tame measures to plug a fiscal gap running at 6.6 percent of gross domestic product.
Alarcon, who confirmed Carrera in his post during the last cabinet crisis in May, has denied rumored plans to hike petrol and natural gas prices as had been promised to foreign investors.
